newsitem.title: FINLAND: Huhtamaki sees further EPS rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Huhtamaki sees further EPS rise in 1997.

text.p: Finnish confectionery and packaging materials group Huhtamaki Oy said on Tuesday it expected earnings per share to improve further this year.
"After a slow start of the year, a further improvement in earnings per share is expected for 1997," Huhtamaki said in a statement with its 1996 results.
Huhtamaki's 1996 EPS rose to 10.29 markka from 7.56 markka the previous year. Group profit after financial items rose 33 percent to 416 million markka.
"Huhtamaki's main Western European markets are likely to develop steadily. Further growth is sought from expanding product segments and the new markets of Eastern Europe and Asia," it said.

Huhtamaki said it would actively pursue company acquisitions to strengthen both its Leaf confectionery and Polarcup packaging businesses. "For this reason alone, any projections for net sales are likely to be wrong," Huhtamaki said.
After the divestment last year of its pharmaceuticals unit Leiras, Huhtamaki said the new group structure would materially change the seasonal pattern of sales and profit generation.

"Operating earnings for the first four months will represent less than a fifth of the annual total, due to Polarcup's strong summer sales and Leaf's higher seasonal sales in the autumn," Huhtamaki said.

At the corporate level, the shift to financial revenue from expenditure -- over three billion markka of capital was freed last year through divestments -- together with rental and royalty income "will boost profit substantially," it said.
"Strong seasonal sales in the second half of 1997 will contribute to another full-year profit improvement," it said.
